study type: Retrospective cohort study with a matched control group
exposure: Surgical treatment for tubal heterotopic pregnancies (HPs)
cohort: The study included 446 patients who conceived tubal heterotopic pregnancies via IVF-ET and underwent surgical treatment, compared to a matched control group of patients with live eutopic singleton pregnancies.
finding: Patients who conceived tubal heterotopic pregnancies and underwent surgical treatment for ectopic pregnancies had similar overall pregnancy outcomes, including live birth, preterm birth, low birth weight, and perinatal mortality, compared to controls, except for a significantly higher caesarean section rate.
mod_finding: The caesarean section rate was significantly higher in the study group (patients who underwent surgical treatment for tubal HPs) compared to the control group.
birth_weight: Birth weight was measured, with low birth weight as an outcome; overall birth weights were similar between groups.
gest_age: Preterm birth was an outcome, indicating gestational age was considered.
